request.spec:
A period may cap the number of open claims per person (a whole number on the period form, blank
for none; PERIOD_ADDED gains cap=<n> at the end when given). Opening a claim that belongs to the
period, alone or by the bulk button, is refused with an error on the claim when the person already
has that many OPEN or PENDING claims in it.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A period may cap the number of open claims per person (a whole number on the period form, blank
for none; PERIOD_ADDED gains cap=<n> at the end when given). Opening a claim that belongs to the
period, alone or by the bulk button, is refused with an error on the claim when the person already
has that many OPEN or PENDING claims in it.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A period can now have a cap on open claims per person, and opening a claim beyond that cap is refused. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

The test spec never actually hits the cap: the claims it opens don't fall in the capped period. So I checked it separately against the running app. On a period with cap 2, the first two opens went through and the third was refused with a 400 and stayed DRAFT. Bulk open uses the same per-claim open call, so it is refused the same way and counted under `bulk-refused`. I didn't check whether the audit file stays clean on a refusal, because my test run's audit file was never written.

**What changed:**
- **Stored data:** a new migration `V81__period_cap.sql` adds a `claim_cap` column to the `period` table. It is empty when there is no cap.
- **Server:**
  - The period form accepts a cap. Blank means no cap; anything other than a whole number of 1 or more (so `0` too) is refused with `period-form-error`.
  - The cap is stored and returned with the period.
  - `PERIOD_ADDED` gets ` cap=<n>` at the end only when a cap is set.
- **Opening a claim** (`ApplyClaimAction.java`): a claim belongs to a period when its due-by date falls in it, the same rule the app already uses for `claim-period`. If that period has a cap and the person already has that many OPEN or PENDING claims due in it, the open is refused. The message shows on the row's existing `claim-error`.
- **Front end** (`Periods.tsx`): a `period-form-cap` field (with the same check in the browser) and a `period-cap` column, which is blank when there is no cap.

Periods made by the "generate" buttons (monthly or fiscal year) never get a cap; only the add-period form sets one.
